newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada and Alberta set C$16.4 mln cattle fund.
newsitem.headline: Canada and Alberta set C$16.4 mln cattle fund.

text.p: The governments of Canada and Alberta on Thursday set aside C$16.4 million for cattle production research, a joint statement said.
The Alberta Cattle Commission will administer the program aimed at production research in Alberta's cow-calf and feedlot sectors. The fund may target research, biotechnology and market development.
"This fund is part of our strategy to promote the long term viability of agriculture...and ensure we continue to be competitive in world markets," Canadian Agriculture Minister Lyle Vanclief said.
Alberta slaughtered 63 percent of Canada's beef from January 1 to May 24, Agriculture Canada statistics show.

"This fund is another tool that will assist the Alberta agri-food industry in achieving its market opportunity of C$10 billion in primary agriculture and C$20 billion in value added processing by 2005," Alberta Agriculture Minister Ed Stelmach said.
A committee of beef cattle producers along with federal and provincial officials will direct the Beef Industry Development Fund, the statement said.
